title: Counting Chargeable Months on Deeply Overdue Refined Fuels and Propane Balances
content:
Once an energy balance under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts has run a long way past its terms, the months the arrears bear a charge for are counted differently, and how the account has been served over the recent quarter decides which count is used.

**Where the days overdue reach 60 and 2 or more stops were made on the account in the three months ending on the handling date**, the months the arrears bear a charge for are the days overdue divided by thirty and carried to four decimal places, a part month counting for the days it ran.

**Where the days overdue reach 60 and fewer than 2 stops were made on the account in that window**, the months the arrears bear a charge for are the whole thirty-day months in the days overdue, with a part month running beyond 15 days counting as a whole month.

**Where the days overdue fall under 60**, the months the arrears bear a charge for are the whole thirty-day months in the days overdue, a part month not counting.

## The three counts set against one another

| Days overdue | Stops made on the account in the three months ending on the handling date | How the months are counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 60 or more | 2 or more | The days overdue divided by thirty, carried to four decimal places; a part month counts for the days it ran |
| 60 or more | Fewer than 2 | Whole thirty-day months, a part month of more than 15 days counting as a whole month |
| Fewer than 60 | Either way | Whole thirty-day months, a part month not counting |

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)

*Seventy days overdue, three stops in the window.* Seventy divided by thirty comes to 2.3333 months, carried to four decimal places.

*Seventy days overdue, one stop in the window.* Seventy days hold 2 whole thirty-day months with 10 days left over. Ten days do not run beyond 15, so the part month is not counted and the months come to 2.

*Eighty days overdue, one stop in the window.* Eighty days hold 2 whole thirty-day months with 20 days left over. Twenty days run beyond 15, so the part month counts as a whole one and the months come to 3.

*Fifty days overdue.* Fifty days hold 1 whole thirty-day month with 20 days left over, which do not count. The months come to 1, whatever the stops in the window.
